fills.narrative: Databricks' June 13 Omnigent is the originating event: a meta-harness wrapping Claude Code, Codex and rival SDKs that enforces cost budgets, permissions and OS-level sandboxing at the wrapping layer across whichever runtime sits underneath. That relocates enterprise-agent governance up to a single vendor-neutral control point, establishing exactly the architectural tier the thesis turns on.
fills.remaining_gap: Only one Databricks instance on the board; a second independent vendor or a governance framework naming the meta-harness as the policy point is still absent.

fills.narrative: Omnigent shipped June 13 as a standalone Apache 2.0 project, not a Databricks-only feature, timed to the Data + AI Summit. Today's coverage reads that as the opening move of an open-core go-to-market, the Spark/Delta playbook, giving away orchestration and policy to seed the default control point while the managed runtime underneath carries durable revenue, establishing the monetization setup.
fills.remaining_gap: No priced, Databricks-hosted tier yet; the counter-risk of staying community OSS and monetizing only via Mosaic AI / Agent Bricks remains fully open.

fills.narrative: The June 12 CacheRL paper is the originating artifact: it removes live tool execution from multi-turn agent RL via three-tier cached-rollout replay plus a cache-aware reward, reporting 92% process accuracy near GPT-5's 94% at ~100x less compute. The bottleneck it cuts is universal and cached replay is a drop-in rollout substitution, the diffusion-prone shape every open post-training library could adopt.
fills.remaining_gap: Technique confined to the single CacheRL paper and its own repo; no second mainstream framework feature or independent reproduction on another base model yet.

fills.narrative: Omnigent wraps command-line agents and rival SDKs behind one interface so implementations swap without rewriting, shipping from a major vendor as Apache 2.0 OSS rather than a research demo. That hard-confirms the underlying force the prediction rides, the market converging on a single abstraction over heterogeneous coding agents, even though Omnigent uses its own wrapping interface and YAML authoring.
fills.remaining_gap: Omnigent is not an adoption of Agent Client Protocol; it proves interop is now first-class without establishing ACP specifically as the default named standard.
